findings.description: `repair_metadata_json` binds `rhs` with `--argjson`, but the value is a plain space-separated string from `sort | tr | sed`, or an empty string when no repair hops were skipped. `jq --argjson rhs ""` and `jq --argjson rhs "claude:over_budget"` are invalid JSON, so envelope construction fails even on normal runs with no skip file.
findings.failure_mode: A review can complete validation and then abort while building metadata, producing no adversarial envelope. With `set -e`, the failed command substitution can terminate the script before `write_output`; without it, later `--argjson repairmeta "$repair_metadata_json"` receives an empty/non-JSON value and fails as well.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `--argjson rhs ...` to `--arg rhs ...` and keep the existing jq expression treating `$rhs` as a string, or emit a real JSON array from the shell and adjust the jq expression accordingly.

findings.description: In the takeover section the verdict `stuck` is emitted whenever `mv -- "$dir" "$_stale"` fails, which conflates two different states: the dead lock directory could not be renamed (permissions), and the directory vanished between the `[[ -d "$dir" ]] || { echo released; }` check and the rename (the holder released unserialised after its own 5 s flock wait, or without flock installed). After the loop, `stuck` is mapped to `_adv_run_lock_unguarded` and the run proceeds. If a `stuck` verdict lands on round 3 and the round-4 `mkdir` then loses to a fresh run that took the freed key, the code reports a dead lock that could not be moved aside and runs unguarded beside a live holder, whereas the same round-4 loss after `takeover`/`released` is correctly refused.
findings.failure_mode: Two live runs for the same (sprint, gate) write the single-writer envelope and sidecars concurrently, in exactly the window the lock exists to close. Requires the vanish-during-section race to occur on round 3 specifically plus a lost round-4 mkdir, so the likelihood is low.
findings.suggested_fix: After the failed `mv`, distinguish the states: `if mv ...; then ...; echo takeover; elif [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then echo released; else echo stuck; fi`. `released` already routes a lost round-4 mkdir to a refusal rather than an unguarded run.
